body.en: The EST II Mathematics subject test is a rigorous examination for students in international and American-diploma programmes who wish to demonstrate advanced mathematical competency for university admissions. It covers algebra, geometry, trigonometry, and data analysis at a depth beyond the core EST I test.

EST II Math is taken as a standalone subject test on the EST II examination day. It contains both multiple-choice and short constructed-response questions. The content aligns closely with pre-calculus and advanced secondary mathematics.

label.en: ⏱ EST II Math Level 1 Pacing & Calculator Strategy

body.en:
• Pacing Baseline: 50 questions in 60 minutes = 72 seconds per question. There is zero negative marking — never leave any question blank.
  • Three-Pass Execution: Pass 1 (Qs 1–25, ~20 min): bank routine algebra, basic trigonometry, and straight arithmetic. Pass 2 (Qs 26–45, ~25 min): solve conic equations, solid geometry, and multi-step probability. Pass 3 (Qs 46–50 & review, ~15 min): tackle non-routine proofs, vectors, and ensure all grid-in/bubble items are complete.
  • Calculator Mastery: An approved scientific or graphing calculator is permitted throughout. Use it to verify complex number computations, evaluate trigonometric functions in proper degree/radian modes, and solve quadratic systems.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 750+ on EST II Math

body.en:
• 1. Never Leave Unanswered Items: With no penalty for incorrect answers, eliminate obvious extremes and make an educated guess whenever stumped.
  • 2. Verify Calculator Angle Mode: Trig questions in EST II frequently switch between radian measure (e.g., \(5\pi/6\)) and degree measure (e.g., \(150°\)). Confirm angle mode before performing numerical evaluations.
  • 3. Conic Identification by Inspection: Check the coefficients of \(x^2\) and \(y^2\): equal signs and equal coefficients indicate a circle; equal signs but different coefficients indicate an ellipse; opposite signs indicate a hyperbola.
  • 4. Memorize 3D Solid & Circle Relations: Sphere volume \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) and surface area \(4\pi r^2\); cone volume \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\); inscribed circle angle \(=\frac{1}{2}\text{central}\); cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to \(180°\).

caption.en: EST II Mathematics domain distribution. Advanced Algebra (20%) and Functions (20%) together form 40% of the exam, complemented by Trigonometry (15%), Sequences & Complex Numbers (10%), Geometry (10%), Circles & Coordinate Geometry (10%), Statistics (10%), and Solid Geometry (5%).

question.en: An EST II Mathematics examination consists of 50 questions with an allocated testing time of 60 minutes. If a student completes the first 30 questions in 33 minutes, what is the maximum average time, in seconds, the student can spend on each of the remaining 20 questions?

solution.en:
Step 1: Compute total available time in seconds: \[ 60\text{ min} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 3600\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 2: Compute time spent on first 30 questions: \[ 33\text{ min} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 1980\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 3: Calculate remaining time: \[ 3600 - 1980 = 1620\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 4: Determine average time per remaining question: \[ \frac{1620\text{ seconds}}{20\text{ questions}} = 81\text{ seconds per question}. \]

question.en: On the EST II Math exam, Advanced Algebra and Functions together account for 40% of the questions. In a 50-question test, if a student targets an accuracy rate of 90% in these two high-yield domains, how many questions from these domains can the student afford to miss at most?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find total questions from Advanced Algebra and Functions: \[ 50 \times 0.40 = 20\text{ questions}. \]

Step 2: Calculate 90% accuracy target: \[ 20 \times 0.90 = 18\text{ questions correct}. \]

Step 3: Find maximum allowed missed questions: \[ 20 - 18 = 2\text{ questions}. \]
